routing_warnings.description: The instruction to gather articles directly from the website concerns content sourcing rather than issue-content completeness.
The supplied images are specifically intended to correct large empty spaces on article pages.
The page-numbered images address empty space on specific article pages rather than the issue's editorial sequence.
This message concerns advertisement resizing, trim, bleed, and safe-zone placement rather than general image-quality enhancement.
The reported blurry assets are specifically advertisements and belong to the advertisement-rendering Requirement.
The advertisement-repair clause may also support the advertisement-rendering Requirement; only the separate low-resolution general-image clause supports the target Requirement.
The missing page-33 image was part of the page-specific additions intended to fill article whitespace, not evidence of low-resolution asset enhancement.
The page-33 fading and positioning treatment concerns page composition and visual pacing rather than repair of a low-quality source image.
The message delivers the PDF intended for Heyzine upload rather than establishing or verifying the hosting and branding arrangement.
The review confirms delivery of files prepared for digital flipbook distribution, not successful hosting or removal of platform branding.
The statement that a print version is unnecessary unless prints are requested changes the print-output Requirement, independently of the launch deadline.
The instruction to insert images only on pages with huge empty spaces concerns whitespace balancing rather than the launch deadline.
The review verifies delivery of files prepared for digital flipbook distribution, but it does not concretely establish that the flipbook went live by the operative launch deadline.
This message concerns breaking up text-heavy articles to avoid reader monotony rather than correcting empty space at article endings.
The proposal to use placeholders, blurbs, and quotes addresses pacing of long text and is better routed to the text-and-visual-pacing Requirement.
This client acceptance resolves the preceding proposal about breaking up long text, not the later article-ending whitespace issue.
The complaint about empty white space at article endings concerns page-ending whitespace balance rather than pacing of long uninterrupted text.
The report of pages with huge empty spaces and the request to fill them with images belongs to the article-ending whitespace Requirement.
The instruction to use only the supplied images and no extra text resolves the whitespace-filling method rather than changing long-text visual pacing.
The resizing, trim, bleed, and unsafe-zone findings concern the narrower advertisement safe-placement Requirement rather than advertisement rendering clarity.
The claimed interactive links between the contents page and chapters concern digital PDF navigation rather than table-of-contents reference accuracy.
